components.name: Probe enclosure
components.purpose: A deliberate grip for low-contact-force imaging, with two controls and a visible status strip.
components.interface: Illustrative envelope: 150 × 56 × 34 mm. Tether routes to a separate acquisition unit.
components.test: Gloved reach, cleaning, balance and contact-force usability studies.

components.name: Ultrasound cartridge
components.purpose: The primary structural imaging channel. Begin with a conventional linear-array module.
components.interface: Candidate 7–15 MHz band; acoustic coupling, receive chain and synchronized acquisition.
components.test: Point-spread function, vessel localization, near-field performance and deformation.

components.name: Photoacoustic rails
components.purpose: Experimental hemoglobin contrast, registered with ultrasound rather than used as an autonomous diagnosis.
components.interface: Tethered laboratory source first. Evaluate 850 nm LEDs and a 1064 nm pulsed-source alternative.
components.test: Incremental benefit over US alone, exposure, heating, pigmentation effects and motion.

components.name: Passive contact shoe
components.purpose: Replaceable interface with an open working corridor and proposed contact-force sensing.
components.interface: Acoustic and optical transmission; no active suction in the initial design.
components.test: Transmission loss, air gaps, vessel compression, cleaning and sterility requirements.

components.name: Acquisition & monitoring
components.purpose: Coordinate acquisition and monitor contact and temperature, with a proposed independent optical interlock.
components.interface: Separate bench source/acquisition unit; the complete system is not contained in this handle.
components.test: Synchronization, registration, failure states, latency, power and thermal budgets.

requirements.verify: Signal, exposure, thermal and acquisition budgets

requirements.meaning: Phantom test positions, not operating-depth claims
requirements.verify: Detection rate and localization error at every depth

requirements.meaning: Phantom sizes, not clinical access thresholds
requirements.verify: Segmentation and diameter error with confidence intervals

requirements.target: Tracked sweep or controlled bench scan
requirements.verify: Registration error, motion sensitivity and coverage
Predefined incremental benefit, failures and added time
Coupling, deformation, cleaning and sterility research
Gloves, motion, lighting, cleaning and usability

requirements.meaning: Never infer a safe vessel from absent data
requirements.verify: Dropout, corruption, calibration and motion cases

claims.finding: LEDX uses visible side-transillumination. NIR camera imaging and PA tomography are different methods.

claims.claim: 15 mm or 25 mm depth is already proven for this design
claims.finding: Published performance is specific to each research setup. Focal length and proposed test depths are not demonstrated VASCOUT operating depths.
Bias remains a research problem; diverse optical conditions and skin pigmentation require explicit evaluation.

claims.claim: The Gemini fusion code is production-ready
claims.finding: Static and scalar review found six failure cases, including depth-only needle containment, empty candidate selection and missing-signal treatment directives. The code is excluded.

claims.claim: The cited AFE chips each have 64/128 channels
claims.finding: AFE5832LP has 32 receive inputs; MAX2082 has eight transceiver channels. A complete channel architecture is unresolved.

claims.claim: The hybrid concept is unprecedented or cleared
claims.finding: PA/US systems and ring sensors have prior art. Patent novelty, regulatory pathway and VASCOUT safety/effectiveness have not been established.

questions.title: Does the added modality help?
questions.prompt: Compare ultrasound alone with registered US + PA using the same task and ground truth.
questions.gate: Measure localization, registration, failed acquisitions and additional time. Predefine what benefit would justify the extra system.

questions.title: Can contact preserve the anatomy?
questions.prompt: Evaluate the passive shoe, force sensing, air gaps and motion across compliant vessel phantoms.
questions.gate: Record vessel deformation and coupling loss. Establish materials, cleaning and sterility requirements.

questions.title: Where does optical contrast fail?
questions.prompt: Vary attenuation, pigmentation, depth, hematoma-like absorbers and illumination geometry.
questions.gate: Report performance by condition. Include UNKNOWN states and uncertainty instead of a universal correction claim.

questions.title: Which objects can be localized?
questions.prompt: Study metal, glass and other relevant materials across sizes, depths and orientations.
questions.gate: Report sensitivity, specificity and localization error. No negative result may imply all fragments have been excluded.

questions.title: Can a trained user interpret it?
questions.prompt: Review gloved controls, attention demands, misleading overlays, motion and low-perfusion use cases with clinicians.
questions.gate: Measure task completion and use errors. Human-factors review precedes claims about field benefit.

questions.title: What evidence would permit human use?
questions.prompt: Define intended use with clinical, regulatory and safety experts before appropriately approved human studies.
questions.gate: Clinical safety, effectiveness, legal pathway and field suitability remain unverified. Reviewed below means discussed, not clinically validated.

sources.title: Veinlite LEDX — directions for use
sources.quote: These plastic covers are not sterile.
sources.supports: Visible side-transillumination; 24 orange and 8 red LEDs. A useful baseline for superficial vessel visibility.
sources.limits: Not NIR camera projection or PA tomography. Manufacturer specifications are not comparative clinical proof. Direct DFU read; exact wavelengths unverified.

sources.title: Photoacoustic vector tomography for deep haemodynamic imaging
sources.quote: an axial resolution of 125 μm and a lateral resolution of 150 μm.
sources.supports: Healthy hand/arm vascular flow measurements deeper than 5 mm in the reported system.
sources.limits: Linear array and fiber delivery, not this probe. The 15 mm focal length is not proven 15 mm human imaging depth. Abstract/figures read; full-text access incomplete.

sources.title: Photoacoustic imaging of human vasculature using LED versus laser illumination
sources.quote: tradeoffs between portability, cost, optical energy and frame rate
sources.supports: 850 nm LED-PAI is published prior work, including phantom and healthy wrist/forearm comparisons.
sources.limits: Mechanically scanned, water-coupled research acquisition is not handheld field validation. No proof of the proposed 120 Hz integrated pipeline. Abstract verified; direct publisher access limited.

sources.title: Monitoring peripheral hemodynamic response to changes in blood pressure via photoacoustic imaging
sources.supports: Peripheral perfusion observations around dialysis and exercise motivate further research.
sources.limits: Not a validated dehydration meter or hemorrhagic-shock classifier. Primary-source retrieval by research reviewer; full article not independently reread by root.

sources.title: Thin ceramic PZT dual- and multi-frequency pMUT arrays for photoacoustic imaging
sources.quote: only 2D photoacoustic images can be reconstructed without depth scanning.
sources.supports: Related ring and square sensor-array prior art tested with pencil leads in agar.
sources.limits: Not a real-time human vascular access device. Novelty and freedom to operate remain unverified. Indexed primary text reviewed; direct PMC access challenged.

sources.title: The confounding effects of skin colour in photoacoustic imaging
sources.quote: no generalisable bias correction has been demonstrated.
sources.supports: Study of 42 healthy participants covering Fitzpatrick I–VI and vitiligo; optical and acoustic confounding affects measurements.
sources.limits: No demonstrated skin-tone invariance for VASCOUT. Direct article read; published 17 June 2026.

sources.title: TCCC Guidelines — vascular access claim audit
sources.supports: The 1 May 2026 guideline provides the clinical context for the vascular-access claim audit.
sources.limits: Its access section does not specify Gemini’s six-second classifier or 1.2 mm vessel threshold. Direct PDF read. This app does not give treatment instructions.

sources.title: Bedside ultrasound for detection of soft tissue foreign bodies: a cadaveric study
sources.supports: In this study: six cadavers, six physicians, 900 examinations; sensitivity 52.6%, specificity 47.2%.
sources.limits: Small objects ≤5 mm at depths ≤3 cm. Results are setting-specific; negative imaging cannot universally exclude fragments. Abstract directly read.

sources.title: Ultrasound evaluation of soft-tissue foreign bodies by US Army medics
sources.supports: After two hours of training, 28 medics studied wooden objects in chicken-thigh models.
sources.limits: Simulated-use evidence, not injured-human or battlefield validation. Primary abstract and indexed article reviewed; direct PMC retrieval limited.

sources.title: Ultrasonography-guided peripheral intravenous access versus traditional approaches
sources.quote: Success rate was greater for the ultrasonographic group (97%) versus control (33%)
sources.supports: Reported benefit in 60 difficult-access patients at two hospitals.
sources.limits: Odd/even-day allocation and two US operators; not concealed randomized assignment. Read alongside S10b. Indexed primary abstract; full article unverified.

sources.title: Ultrasonographically guided peripheral intravenous cannulation: a randomized trial
sources.quote: Superiority of ultrasonographically guided peripheral intravenous cannulation is not supported by this study.
sources.supports: A 59-patient ED trial did not demonstrate improvement in attempts, time or satisfaction.
sources.limits: Conflicting evidence matters; results depend on workflow and setting. Indexed primary abstract; full article unverified.

sources.title: FDA: Imagio Breast Imaging System — P200003
sources.quote: uses both optoacoustic (OA) and ultrasound (US) to image breast tissues
sources.supports: An approved OA/US product exists for a specified breast-imaging indication.
sources.limits: Unrelated indication: no VASCOUT clearance, safety/effectiveness or predetermined legal pathway follows. Direct FDA overview read.

sources.title: A device for improving the visual clarity and dimension of veins
sources.supports: Related vacuum-device research used a healthy-volunteer crossover study.
sources.limits: Not shock patients; does not establish the Gemini suction range or outcome. Indexed abstract reviewed; repository/PDF fetch gaps. Suction excluded from initial concept.

sources.title: TI AFE5832LP — ultrasound analog front end
sources.supports: 32 receive inputs with 16 multiplexed ADC channels.
sources.limits: Not a single 64/128-channel transceiver. Complete transmit/receive architecture, bandwidth and power budget are unresolved. Direct manufacturer page read.

sources.title: Analog Devices MAX2082 — octal ultrasound transceiver
sources.supports: Eight channels per device, with integrated transmit and receive functions.
sources.limits: Does not establish feasibility of the proposed 128-channel dual-band C-ring. Direct manufacturer page read.

sources.title: User-supplied Gemini concepts — audited research inputs
sources.supports: Motivating ideas: visible vascular mapping, field access, LED-PAI and a possible C-ring geometry.
sources.limits: Two supplied PDFs and three text attachments are proposals, not studies. Six latest-code failure cases were reproduced using independent arithmetic; no supplied code was executed. No autonomous diagnosis or treatment logic adopted.
